topic: Time a CUDA kernel correctly: why a host wall-clock timer over-reports and a same-stream event does not.
goal: State why a same-stream CUDA event measures device progress while a host wall clock measures enqueue latency.
grill: I want to time a matmul kernel on my H100 and compare it with cuBLAS.
I will run it on the homelab GPU and report GFLOP/s.
I can compute GFLOP/s from the formula, but I do not trust my timings.

facts.claim: The host launches kernels asynchronously, so the launch returns before the kernel finishes.
A CUDA event is recorded in a stream and timestamped when the stream reaches it.
A kernel launch is written into a stream, and the device consumes that stream.
A host timer measures the enqueue cost, because the kernel runs later; only an in-stream event measures device progress.
facts.wrong: A host wall-clock timer around the launch measures how long the kernel ran on the device.

commandOutput: matmul: 0.42 ms (host wall clock) / 0.97 ms (CUDA event pair)
